Consider the following requirements:

Client is the computer to be backed up.
Server is the computer hosting the backup.

Client should back up its contents on a schedule.
Client should back up so that physical access during a backup is no more dangerous than any other time when it's running but locked.
Client must send the backup over the wire encrypted- the network need not be trusted.

Physical access to server at any time should not allow recovery of any of the stored backups without an encryption key.

Client's backup should be a full system backup. i.e. in case of failure of client, another machine with at least as much hard disk space can be imaged.
Client's backup on the server should be browsable on the file level, so that any one file can be backed up individually and conveniently.

And... these should be incremental backups, so 5 TB won't take all day or month.
